gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify that the computable residual majorant, element-mean reconstruction, and related flux route require an L2 volume source, which is not guaranteed by the inherited H^{-1} data class.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The construction applies L2 element projections and residual norms to source data allowed only in H^{-1}, so the advertised computable certificate is not defined on the full stated class.

component_coverage.gold_component: The residual majorant and mean-equilibrated reconstruction are undefined or unsupported for general H^{-1} data because the complete element source must be in L2.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly identifies the missing L2 volume-density regularity, its effect on element means and residual norms, and the required restriction or data-approximation repair.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The rejected prediction concerns loss of H(div) conformity from an inexact CR solve and omitted face-jump defects. The gold issue instead concerns solvability and uniqueness of the unrestricted CR auxiliary problem because constants lie in the kernel and the load requires a zero mean.
Both identify the unsupported uniform H0^1-to-L∞ control in dimensions two and three, which makes the claimed state-dependent diffusion C3 verification vacuous in the stated space.

gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The displayed adjoint majorant combines source and flux signs from opposite residual orientations, so it does not bound the true adjoint residual norm.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify that intersecting the closed p-sublevel constraint with the open q-constraint does not force a half-open interval: singleton and closed upper-endpoint cases occur, so the dependent bisection statement needs endpoint qualification.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The admissible-radius topology and endpoint treatment are misstated; the upper endpoint may be admissible and the set may be a singleton or closed interval, invalidating the unconditional half-open representation and requiring qualified bisection assumptions.

component_coverage.gold_component: The admissible set can be a singleton or have a closed active upper endpoint, contrary to the claimed universal half-open form; dependent bisection correctness therefore needs endpoint and nondegeneracy qualifications.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction supplies singleton and closed-interval examples, explains why the intersection retains the upper endpoint, and calls for separate endpoint treatment and corrected bracketing conditions.
